# SEO-017: Serve the site from one production HTTPS origin

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

Exactly one scheme-and-host pair serves public content. Every other host or scheme that resolves for the site issues a permanent redirect to that origin rather than serving a second copy of the same pages.

## Rationale

When more than one origin serves the same pages, every URL exists more than once, external link signals are split across the copies, and the search engine rather than the site decides which origin represents the content.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_production_origin"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Find where the deployment terminates TLS and resolves hostnames, declare the chosen origin once in configuration, and redirect the remaining hostnames and the http scheme to it with 301. Do not add application-level redirects if the hosting platform already owns hostname routing.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Request each hostname and scheme that resolves for the site and record the full redirect chain and final URL for every one of them.
- Evidence: `REDIRECT_CHAIN`, `HTTP_STATUS`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: none.

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
